executionPlan: Root-caused the pop and fixed it at the source: (1) three's fadeOut/fadeIn restart from weight 1/0, so a fall cut short by touchdown snapped the pelvis 0.3 m in one frame (also with the pass off); crossfades now start from the current weight. (2) The landing crouch is sampled once from the real animator on a bone copy; during the fall the push is built before touchdown, and where the crouch needs more than 0.2 m of push (or the player walks into the wall during it) the animator plays the soft landing. (3) Whatever correction remains is rate-limited (2.2 m/s), the offset is capped at 0.299 m, the legs and feet are probed, and the solve is tiered (hard 0.05 m at the joints first, comfort margin and hands only with what is left). Verified with a 1920-run physics+animator sweep, mutation checks, a production build in a copy and a real-GPU Chrome A/B against a pass-off control build.
summary: F-M3-3 is fixed at the source: no pop (unit sweep max offset change 2.2 m/s over 1920 runs, was 4 to 20 m/s; browser max 2.62 m/s except one frame at 3.05 m/s that is a 11.9 ms render-interval artifact), total offset 0.299 m, hard landing kept where there is room, soft landing near walls. Clearance now covers legs and feet and is far better than the control (unit: 8 of 1920 runs short, worst 7 mm from a surface, control 987 runs and 0.64 m inside; browser: 0 to 25 frames per run under 0.05 m, worst toe 6.6 cm inside, control 130 to 196 frames and up to 30 cm inside) but it is NOT fully met: the 0.3 m offset cap and the 0.05 m clearance conflict in corners, so criteria 1 (one browser frame) and 2 (browser frames, Lab plinth toes) are reported failed.

criteria.criterion: F-M3-3 is fixed: the visual root offset never changes faster than 3 m/s relative to the physics position on any frame (no single-frame pop), measured per frame in a unit test that drives real physics and the real animator through jumps and hard landings pressed against at least 20 generated wall and prop faces, and in the browser on the production build in QA's lab-side-l-inner, lab-kiosk, lab plinth and workshop machine scenarios over 4 runs each; the approach anticipates poses that reach forward (for example measuring the landing pose ahead of time, choosing the soft landing, or limiting lean near solids) instead of correcting after the fact.
criteria.evidence: Unit: passes strictly (bodyClearance.test.ts, 109 generated faces x 6 poses x jumps, hard drop, run-jump; max rate 2.2 m/s, was 4 to 20 m/s; a dedicated test shows the push is already 85 percent in place at touchdown, and the test fails with anticipation or the rate limit disabled). Browser (5 spots incl. 2 lab plinths, 4 runs each): max 2.62 m/s on 99.99 percent of frames, but ONE frame measures 3.05 m/s (lab-plinth-apex run 0) because the render timestamp interval was 11.9 ms against the 16.7 ms step the pass used; the pass step itself is 2.2 m/s times its dt. Earlier builds in this session also showed single 3.4 and 3.67 samples at 9.6 to 13.6 ms intervals, so 2.2 leaves about 35 percent headroom for frame jitter but not a guarantee. The anticipation itself is implemented as asked: the landing crouch is sampled from the real animator ahead of time, the push is built during the fall, the soft landing is chosen where the crouch needs more than 0.2 m of push, a crouch is cut short when the player walks into a wall, and the root cause (crossfade restarting from weight 1) is fixed.

assumptions: Blocks whose top is at most 0.95 m above the floor under the avatar (jump height 0.9 m plus 0.05) are something to step or jump onto: legs and feet are not kept clear of them; head, neck, chest and hips always are. The Lab plinths (1.0 m), kiosk (1.1 m) and machines stay covered.

A foot above the top face of a block minus 0.06 m stands on it (the colliders leave the soles a few cm under the visible top, and a capsule resting on an edge sits up to 0.13 m low); ramps and steps are walked on.
The 0.3 m offset cap takes priority over 0.05 m clearance where they conflict (corners), because the contract states both and the cap is the visible-artifact guard.
Browser rate is measured on render-hook timestamps like QA's harness; the pass uses the game's own frame delta, so display jitter shows up as measured rate variation.
The pass-off control build disables the pass but keeps the new animator crossfade, so A/B isolates the pass; the pre-fix pop was reproduced separately in a unit test.
decisionsProposed: Decision for the user on the residual conflict in corners (Lab plinths, kiosk and machine corners pressed diagonally): (A) accept the current state, toes or knees up to about 6 cm into a prop for a few frames at the 0.3 m cap; (B) allow the offset to exceed 0.3 m only in a squeeze (up to about 0.4 m), which is expected to remove the browser shortfalls at the cost of criterion 3 as written; (C) add 0.1 m of physical standoff to the capsule or the colliders, which removes the need for the push at the source but touches physics, doorway widths and camera pocket tests.
Keep crossfades in the animator driven by its own per-action weights instead of three's fadeIn/fadeOut (the latter restart from weight 1 and 0 when a fade is interrupted).
lessonsProposed: three.js fadeIn/fadeOut always schedule from weight 1/0: an interrupted crossfade pops the pose to the fading clip at full weight (0.3 m pelvis in one frame after a 5-frame fall). Drive weights from the current value and test short states.

A reactive visual correction cannot be both fast and rate-limited: anticipate (sample the pose from the real animator on a bone copy, look ahead along the velocity, pick the soft variant) and only then rate-limit the remainder; a slow release (1.5 per s) stops the offset from chasing every leg swing.

Margin-based constraints (radius plus 0.05) are infeasible in corners where the 0.05 m acceptance at the joint is feasible: solve the hard 0.05 m tier first, then add comfort margin only if the hard tier does not get worse, and cull points by solid bounds (apply cost went from 1.3 ms to 0.16 ms per call).

Test harness fidelity matters: a facing snap when blocked, setup frames after a teleport and standing on an edge with the capsule sphere (feet up to 0.13 m below the visible top) created false failures that look like pass bugs.
QA check suggestion: measure offset speed on game-time deltas as well as render timestamps, since render intervals jitter between 9 and 17 ms on a 60 Hz display.
